transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, uh… I’m here because the clinic for this logistics job said my weight was too low to clear me. I don’t really see it that way, though. I mean, I’ve always figured I’m just lean—like, ready to work, quick on my feet, you know? But they said I needed to come in and get checked, so… here I am.
Have you been trying to lose weight?

I wouldn’t say I’m trying to lose weight exactly… I just try to keep things light, you know, practical. Most days it’s black coffee, maybe a boiled egg or a little tuna. If I’m not moving freight that shift, I tell myself I don’t really need a full meal. I mean, that makes sense, right?
Are you worried about gaining weight?

I mean… “worried” sounds a little strong, maybe. I just like to keep an eye on it. If I eat something like rice or bread, or anything greasy, I start thinking it’s going to sit on me right away. Then the next morning I’ll check the scale, or see how my belt feels, just to make sure I haven’t… you know, let myself go. Is that what you mean?
Do you fear gaining weight?

I guess… yes, a bit. I don’t like saying “fear,” because that makes it sound dramatic, but if I eat rice or bread or something greasy, I do start thinking it’s going to sit on me right away. Then I’ll check the scale the next morning, or my belt, just to make sure I haven’t let myself go. Does that… answer it?
Have you lost a significant amount of weight recently?

I guess it depends what you’d call significant. The clinic for that logistics job sent me here because they said my weight was too low to clear me. But I don’t know… to me I just look lean, like somebody who’s ready to work and stay quick on his feet. Is that… the kind of thing you’re asking?
Do you think you look underweight when you look in the mirror?

I don’t know if I’d say underweight exactly… I mean, I notice my stomach and my waist mostly. If they don’t look smaller, tight, controlled, then I feel like I’m not the disciplined guy I used to be on the warehouse floor. Maybe that sounds strange, but that’s kind of where my eyes go in the mirror.
Have you experienced any changes in your menstrual cycle?
Um… I’m a man, so I don’t have a menstrual cycle. Unless you mean some other kind of hormone thing? I’m sorry, I just want to make sure I’m answering what you’re asking.
Do you know anyone, such as a female friend or family member, who has experienced changes in their menstrual cycle, such as skipped periods, as a result of being underweight?

I can’t really say I know anyone like that, no. I mean, I’ve heard people talk about skipped periods in general, but not someone close to me where I knew it was because of being underweight. Sorry, I don’t want to guess and give you the wrong answer.
Do you think you would be happier if you were a bit heavier

I want to say yes because I know that probably sounds like the healthier answer… but honestly, I don’t think I’d feel happier. When I look in the mirror, especially at my stomach and waist, if I’m not smaller and tight-looking, I feel like I’ve let myself go somehow… like I’m not that disciplined guy I used to be on the warehouse floor. I know that may not make much sense, but that’s how it feels.
Do you think your weight or eating habits have affected your sex drive or ability to function sexually?

Um… I’m not totally sure how to answer that. I haven’t really been focusing on that part of things much lately. I guess I wouldn’t say I’ve noticed a clear problem, but… I’m not sure if I’d connect anything directly to my weight or eating. Does that make sense?
Do you think you would eat more if you didn't worry about gaining weight?

Yeah… I mean, probably. I don’t like admitting that, because I know it sounds kind of… not right.

If I wasn’t worried about gaining weight, I think I’d be able to eat more normal things. Like rice or bread, or something greasy, I guess. But when I do, I can’t stop thinking it’s going to sit on me right away. Then the next morning I’ll check the scale or even my belt, just to make sure I didn’t… let myself go. Is that what you mean?
Does worrying about gaining weight interfere with your daily activities or thoughts?

Yeah… I guess it does, more than I’d like to admit. I try not to make a big deal of it, but if I eat something like rice or bread, or anything greasy, it kind of stays in my head. I’ll be thinking, “That’s going to sit on me,” like right away.

And then the next morning I’ll usually check the scale, or even how my belt feels, just to make sure I didn’t… you know, let myself go. I know that probably sounds a bit much, but that’s what happens.
Is your fear of gaining weight the main reason you restrict what you eat?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t like saying it that plainly, but that’s probably the main thing.

It’s not like I’m trying to be difficult about food. It’s just, if I eat rice or bread or something greasy, I start thinking it’s going to sit on me right away. Then the next morning I’ll check the scale, or how my belt feels, just to make sure I didn’t let myself go. So… yeah, I guess the fear of gaining weight is a big part of why I hold back. Does that answer it okay?
Do you think you look fat even when others tell you that you are underweight?

I… yeah, sometimes. I know people say I’m underweight, and I’m not trying to argue with them exactly.

But when I look in the mirror, especially around my stomach and waist, it doesn’t look right to me. If I’m not smaller there, kind of tight-looking, I feel like I’ve lost discipline… like I’m not the same man I used to be when I was working hard on the warehouse floor.

I know that may not make sense from the outside. I’m just trying to explain it honestly. Is that what you mean?
Do you think your weight is low even when you look at yourself in the mirror?

I mean… I can see I’m not a big guy right now, sure. I’m not trying to be stubborn about that.

But when my sister and the doctor say I’m in danger, I guess part of me feels like they’re making it bigger than it is. To me it feels more like I’m keeping myself light, you know… sharp, ready for work. Like if I let myself get heavier, I won’t be as capable.

So… I don’t know if I see it the same way they do when I look in the mirror. Does that make sense?
Do you think your weight is normal even when others tell you it's too low?

I guess… yeah, I do think of it as more normal than they do.

My sister and the doctor keep saying it’s too low, that I’m in danger, and I hear them. I’m not trying to dismiss it. But part of me thinks maybe they’re making it bigger than it is, because they don’t really understand that I’m just trying to stay light… sharp… ready for work.

I know that probably sounds like I’m not taking it seriously enough. I’m trying to answer honestly. Is that okay?
Do you think your weight is low even when you look at yourself in the mirror and others tell you it's too low?

I… I guess I don’t see it as low in the same way they do.

When I look at myself, I can tell I’m thinner, but my sister and the doctor keep saying I’m in danger, and part of me feels like they’re maybe making it bigger than it is. I don’t mean that disrespectfully. I just think they don’t understand that I’m trying to keep myself light and sharp, ready for work.

Maybe that sounds like I’m not hearing them enough… but that’s honestly how it feels to me.
Do you think about your weight or fear of gaining weight every day?

Yeah… I guess I do think about it most days. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but it’s kind of there in the back of my mind.

Like if I eat rice or bread, or something greasy, I start thinking it’s going to sit on me right away. Then the next morning I might check the scale, or even just my belt, to make sure I didn’t… you know, let myself go.

I know that probably sounds excessive. I’m just trying to be honest.
Do you think your weight is normal for your body, even when you are underweight according to medical standards?

I mean… I know the medical numbers say I’m under, and I’m not trying to argue with you.

But in my head, it doesn’t feel as extreme as everyone’s saying. My sister and the doctor keep telling me I’m in danger, and I hear that, I do… I just keep thinking maybe they’re making it bigger than it is because they don’t understand why I’m doing it.

I’m trying to keep myself light, sharp, ready for work. So… yeah, I guess part of me still thinks it’s normal for me, even if you’d say it isn’t. Is that a bad answer?
Do you think your weight is low even when you look at yourself in the mirror and feel like you look normal or even overweight?

I know you’ve asked me this a couple ways, and I’m trying to answer it right.

When I look in the mirror, I don’t really see “dangerously low.” I can see I’m not big, but I don’t feel like it’s as bad as my sister and the doctor keep saying. They keep telling me I’m in danger, and I hear them… I just keep thinking maybe they’re making it bigger than it is.

To me, it feels like I’m keeping myself light and sharp, you know, ready for work. I don’t know if that’s the wrong way to see it, but that’s honestly what goes through my mind.
